# Press Feedback

<!-- Generated by generate-swiftui-skill.py; edit the library sources. -->

Category: Feedback

Use ButtonStyle’s isPressed for immediate touch-down feedback, then a quiet spring on release. A 0.97 scale is an illustrative starting point. With Reduce Motion, retain an opacity change without scaling.

- Before: Button stays still while pressed
- After: Press responds before release

APIs: `ButtonStyle`, `isPressed`, `snappy`, `scaleEffect`

## Complete improved example

Adapt the behavior to the app; demonstration controls and values are illustrative.

```swift
import SwiftUI

// iOS 17+. Press and hold the button to compare touch-down feedback.
struct PressFeedbackDoExample: View {
    @State private var count = 0

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 12) {
            Button { count += 1 } label: {
                Label("Add item", systemImage: "plus")
                    .padding(.horizontal, 16)
                    .frame(minHeight: 44)
                    .background(.tint.opacity(0.15), in: .capsule)
                    .contentShape(.capsule)
            }
            .buttonStyle(PressFeedbackStyle())
            Text("Added: \(count)").monospacedDigit()
            Text("Press and hold").font(.caption)
        }
    }
}

// excerpt:start
struct PressFeedbackStyle: ButtonStyle {
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func makeBody(configuration: Configuration) -> some View {
        configuration.label
            .opacity(configuration.isPressed ? 0.75 : 1)
            .scaleEffect(configuration.isPressed && !reduceMotion ? 0.97 : 1)
            .animation(
                reduceMotion || configuration.isPressed ? nil : .snappy(duration: 0.25),
                value: configuration.isPressed
            )
    }
}
// excerpt:end
```
